Maria Chen: heads up — CI is failing on new attention kernels, binary size spiked ~18% on linux-x86_64-gpu build.
Sam Ortiz: saw that, looks like nvcc default changed. which flags are we using?
Maria Chen: compile log: ```nvcc -O3 -gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -lineinfo -Xfatbin -compress-all -fmad=true -use_fast_math -rdc=true``` then size: libkernels.so 134MB -> 158MB
Lee Park: maybe PTX codegen switched to a newer ptx version that expands sections. check the output of `--generate-code` lists. Also we recently enabled `-rdc=true`.
Anton Ivanov: relocatable device code (-rdc) and fatbins increase size. we can try `-rdc=false` for kernel-only builds, but that breaks if we rely on device link-time. another option is split compilation: compile device libs separately and link.
Julia Nguyen: We should gate size regression in CI and add a per-arch size baseline. propose: per-arch baseline + 10% threshold, fail otherwise. keep it simple for now.
Maria Chen: Agree. Also need to lock PTX versions per CUDA toolkit: toolkit 12 should target ptx 7.0+ for sm_80, but older toolchains emit different ptx that new tools expand differently. we should maintain an arch whitelist per toolchain.
Sam Ortiz: Action items: (1) add size-gate job in CI (owner: Sam) (2) try removing -rdc or split compile units (owner: Lee) (3) add step to dump `cuobjdump --list-arch` for artifacts (owner: Maria) (4) document recommended nvcc flags in eng-runtime README (owner: Anton)
ci-bot: new job added: build-kernels-size-check on branch `main` (status: queued)
deploy-bot: @Maria Chen scheduled nightly bisect job at 03:00 UTC
Maria Chen: thanks — I'll start a bisect, ping if you need me to repro locally: docker image `reg.redwood/test-toolchain:cuda12`
Sam Ortiz: cool, keeping short notes in the RFC follow-up doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/serving-kernel-selection#ci
Julia Nguyen: reminder: keep quantization kernels separate from generic attention kernels — quant ops often change codegen patterns and blow up fatbins. :memo:
Lee Park: I'll open a tiny PR to try `--relocatable-device-code=false` and report size diff (w/ numbers).
Anton Ivanov: If that still fails, consider toggling `--generate-line-info` and `-lineinfo`; those sometimes add big debug sections. also `--compress-all` vs none can change fit.
Maria Chen: ok syncing ops tomorrow 11am PT. I'll collate size baselines and links. thanks all :thumbsup:
